title: Tiered backoff and proactive quarantine playbook for asymmetric multi-region SLO miss
text:
Tiered backoff and proactive quarantine playbook for asymmetric multi-region SLO miss

description:
Summary: On 2026-03-04 21:14 UTC a regional SLO miss occurred affecting region-us-west-2 and then amplified during cross-region failover. The visible symptom was sustained elevation of p99 generation latency (SLO threshold = 450ms, observed p99 peaked at ~1.3s) for ~2 hours for a subset of customers. Root cause was a combination of asymmetric traffic fanout after a maintenance window, an overly aggressive circuit-breaker hysteresis that prevented graceful re-attachment of warm KV caches, and a single noisy tenant that consumed disproportionate batching capacity. The combination caused preferential routing to secondary capacity which then tripped a second-tier CB and triggered broad failover cascades and delayed KV cache warmups. This ticket collects the postmortem findings, decisions, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

postmortem_summary:
Two-hour SLO miss driven by asymmetric failover and cascading circuit-breaker hysteresis. Immediate mitigation (manual routing reweight + temporary tenant throttling) restored p99 within 25 minutes. We recommend a three-pronged fix: 1) tiered backoff policy for noisy tenants, 2) conservative CB hysteresis and staggered re-probe, 3) proactive quarantine with warmup isolation to avoid KV cache cold storms.

timeline:
2026-03-04 20:55 UTC - Planned maintenance completed in eu-west-1; control-plane traffic rebalanced
2026-03-04 21:14 UTC - Region us-west-2 p99 begins rising; first alerts triggered by runtime SLO monitor
2026-03-04 21:22 UTC - Circuit breaker CB-A (regional priority) tripped for a set of hotspots; automated failover to secondary pool initiated
2026-03-04 21:27 UTC - Secondary pool experiences KV cache misses; p99 further increases as batching saturates
2026-03-04 21:45 UTC - Manual temporary routing reweight applied and noisy tenant throttled (tenant-T12); p99 trending down
2026-03-04 22:05 UTC - KV caches warmed for hot prefixes; system returns to baseline by 22:20 UTC

root_cause_analysis:
Asymmetric traffic shift: a maintenance-induced rebalancing sent extra fanout to us-west-2 causing uneven request distribution
Circuit breaker hysteresis: CB-A used a single global backoff timer and aggressive reopen thresholds which synchronized retries across many hosts
Noisy tenant hotspot: tenant-T12 issued many short-context high-frequency generation calls causing batching starvation and KV churn
KV cache coldstart amplification: when failover moved traffic, many workers saw cache misses simultaneously leading to sustained higher compute and longer kernel selection latency
Routing policy mismatch: policy allowed immediate failover to capacity without staged ramp-up or token-aware admission control

mitigations_taken:
Applied manual reweighting of routing policies to reduce immediate load on secondary pool
Enacted emergency throttling for tenant-T12 via per-tenant rate limiter for 40 minutes
Increased CB-A reopen interval to avoid synchronized retries during the incident (temporary)
Engaged on-call infra and shard teams; monitored KV cache warmup metrics and token-level latency dashboards

action_items:
AI-1: Implement tiered backoff per-tenant with token-awareness to prioritize high-value requests; owner: Diego Marquez; estimate: 5; due: 2026-03-24
AI-2: Change CB hysteresis to exponential backoff with jitter and add staggered re-probe across hosts; owner: Priya Kapoor; estimate: 3; due: 2026-03-18
AI-3: Add noisy-tenant detector and automated soft-quarantine that preserves KV cache affinity while shedding batch slots; owner: Marco L.; estimate: 8; due: 2026-03-31
AI-4: Routing policy change to staged failover (configurable ramp window + admission control) with a canary for 5% traffic; owner: SRE Team; estimate: 5; due: 2026-03-20
AI-5: Improve KV cache warmup by prefetching top-100 prefixes on failover and expose warmup progress to dashboards; owner: Runtime Team; estimate: 5; due: 2026-04-01
AI-6: Add test harness for multi-region failover simulation to CI (infrastructure test); owner: Infra QA; estimate: 8; due: 2026-04-10

review_feedback:
PM review (Lydia): Prioritize AI-1 and AI-3 for Q2 roadmap; ensure tenant throttling has SLA guardrails
Design review (Evelyn): UX for quarantine notifications to customers should include reason, expected duration, and recovery steps
Security review (Alex): Confirmed quarantine actions don't circumvent audit logging; no blocker
SRE review (Ming): Suggest instrumenting batch-utilization by tenant and adding a historical baseline to alert tuning

comments:
2026-03-05 - Diego M: Draft postmortem completed; requesting review from runtime and routing leads.
2026-03-06 - Priya K (Runtime): Observed that kernel-selection spikes correlated with GPU-migration events; opened GH PR to add guardrail for kernel switches. PR: https://github.com/redwoodai/runtime/pull/4142
2026-03-07 - Marco L (Routing): Proposed staged ramp-up for failover with a 30s ramp window and token-aware admission. Added proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Failover+Ramp+Proposal
2026-03-08 - Security: no sensitive data exposure detected; audit logs intact
2026-03-09 - Ops: Recommend adding a noisy-tenant detection alert based on batch-utilization and per-tenant QPS
